subject: Dedicated sizing: traffic snapshot & response-length breakdown for Signal Retail
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@signal-retail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex@signal-retail.com>
Date: 2029-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing help — sample traffic attached

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — we’re exploring Redwood Dedicated for a transactional retail assistant that will serve checkout and order-status intents. I attached a 48-hour sample export (signal_traffic_sample.csv) with timestamps and minimal payloads. High-level details:
- Peak concurrent active sessions: we currently see spikes to ~1,200 sessions across regions (US primarily).
- Typical prompt mix: order-status (45%), product-recommendation (30%), checkout-assist (25%).
- Avg user prompt length ~18 tokens, expected model response avg ~120 tokens but some receipts/confirmations go up to ~420 tokens.
- Target p95 latency: <= 300ms for short flows, p99 <= 800ms.

Can you help us map this to a dedicated fleet suggestion (GPU SKUs, number of instances, expected throughput)? We can share token histograms or longer traces if that helps.

Appreciate a rough ballpark and what additional artifacts you need.

Best,
Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Platform
Signal Retail

Attachment: signal_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 4800 rows)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@signal-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-07-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — sample traffic attached

Hi Tara — thanks for the sample, that’s exactly the right start. Quick notes and a small checklist so we can produce a conservative Dedicated sizing recommendation: 

1) Token distributions: can you confirm token-per-prompt histogram (0-32, 33-128, 129-512, >512)? If you can’t, we’ll approximate from the CSV but an explicit histogram speeds up accuracy.
2) Response length tails: you mentioned up to ~420 tokens — do receipts/confirmations happen in ~1% of requests or more?
3) Session model: are sessions sticky to users (long-lived multi-turn) or largely single-request per session? If multi-turn, provide avg session steps and KV-cache reuse rates.
4) Retry/error rates and client-side timeouts — important for occupancy assumptions.
5) Desired SLO mapping: is p99 acceptable at 800ms across all intents or only for short flows?

Operational knobs we’ll tune in the sizing: model variant (e.g., gpt-3.5-ish vs larger open weights), quantization (int8/4-bit), batch-window latency targets, KV prefix caching (saves decode tokens on multi-turn flows), and autoscale headroom for burst windows.

I attached our redwood_sizing_template.csv — fill token histograms and session shapes if you can. If not, send a 24-72h token histogram export and we’ll pivot. We’ll run a back-of-envelope once we have the histogram; Marissa and Ben will add the initial fleet estimate.

Available for a 30-min sync Tuesday or Wednesday (PST).

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sizing_template.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara@signal-retail.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-07-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — sample traffic attached

Hi Tara — I pulled the CSV and sketched a back-of-envelope for conservative baseline sizing. Assumptions (call out so we’re explicit):
- Baseline model: 13B open-weights variant, quantized to int8 with decoder-optimized kernels.
- Avg prompt tokens: 18; avg response tokens: 120; 2% of responses >400 tokens (these are heavier tail).
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,200 (as reported); assume 20% multi-turn reuse so KV cache reduces decode tokens by ~15% on average.
- Target p95 latency: 250ms (short flows) and p99 target 750ms.

Estimate (conservative, single-region):
- H100-style instance (1 GPU) effective QPS for this model+quant: ~180 qps sustained with p95 ~250ms when batching window tuned to 15ms and small-request priority.
- To cover 1,200 concurrent with average RTT and 120-response token decode cost, we estimate needing ~7-8 H100 GPUs (or ~12 A100-80GB equivalents) to hit p95 targets with 20-25% buffer for headroom.

If Signal prefers to optimize for cost over strict p95, we can trade to 4-5 H100s with queuing for non-critical flows and traffic-class routing (checkout intents pinned to low-latency pool; recommendations to warm cache pool).

Attachments: back_of_envelope.xlsx (simple throughput math and occupancy sheet).

Next steps: if you can fill the token histogram and confirm the percent of long-form responses, we’ll produce a formal Dedicated sizing PDF with SKU mixes (H100 vs A100 vs GPUT types), expected monthly token cost, and suggested autoscale/canary policies. Happy to run a short lab trial (24–48h) with a pinned fleet if you want live metrics.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tara Singh <tara@signal-retail.com>

I attached a short token histogram export (we’ll send the full 7-day histogram tomorrow) and clarified: long responses (receipts/confirmations) are ~1.6% of volume, and sessions are a mix — ~70% single-turn, ~30% multi-turn with average 3 turns when multi-turn.

We’d like the formal PDF and SKU mix; please schedule the 30-min sync Wednesday 10:30am PST. We’re also open to the 24–48h lab trial you mentioned — we’ll include an NDA addendum if needed.

Best,
Tara
